title: Complaint route timing, visibility, and response categories differ sharply by financial product
source_unit: Capped retrieval-order sample of published CFPB complaint records with case-level route fields
geography: United States complaint records; consumer state and ZIP are reported fields

observations.period: 2024 complaints received; checking or savings account; 500 sampled records

denominator.unit: capped retrieval-order sample; 52,901 total API-matching records

observations.method: Official CFPB complaint API case-level retrieval with date_received_min/max, exact product filter, and size=500; receipt-to-company-send lag computed from date_received and date_sent_to_company.
observations.uncertainty: Capped retrieval-order sample; no sampling standard error or weighting. Date sent is routing to the company, not company response completion or verified remedy.
observations.subgroup: Published complaints identified as checking or savings account complaints.
observations.counterinterpretation: Product issue mix, company mix, complaint propensity, route access, and publication rules can produce the pattern; response labels do not measure restored money, time, or trust.

observations.period: 2024 complaints received; credit reporting or other personal consumer reports; 500 sampled records

denominator.unit: capped retrieval-order sample; 2,370,336 total API-matching records

observations.method: Same CFPB case-level procedure and capped retrieval-order sample as the adjacent product observation.
observations.uncertainty: Capped retrieval-order sample; no sampling standard error or weighting. The very large product universe is not represented by 500 cases as a population estimate.
observations.subgroup: Published complaints identified as credit reporting or other personal consumer report complaints.
observations.counterinterpretation: Rapid routing may reflect product-specific system integration rather than consumer access or resolution; non-monetary relief and explanation remain company/administrative labels.

denominator.unit: capped retrieval-order sample; 21,474 total API-matching records

observations.method: Same CFPB case-level procedure and capped retrieval-order sample as the adjacent product observation.
observations.uncertainty: Capped retrieval-order sample; no sampling standard error or weighting. Routing tail does not measure company response delay or mortgage outcome.
observations.subgroup: Published complaints identified as mortgage complaints.
observations.counterinterpretation: Mortgage product and issue complexity, company routing, weekends, and publication timing may shape the long tail; explanation is not proof of correction.

observations.period: 2024 complaints received; student loan; 500 sampled records

denominator.unit: capped retrieval-order sample; 14,685 total API-matching records

observations.method: Same CFPB case-level procedure and capped retrieval-order sample as the adjacent product observation.
observations.uncertainty: Capped retrieval-order sample; no sampling standard error or weighting. Routing delay is not company resolution delay, and explanation is not a verified remedy.
observations.subgroup: Published complaints identified as student-loan complaints.
observations.counterinterpretation: Product-specific servicing, transfer, legal, and administrative complexity may produce the routing tail and response mix; public response visibility is optional.

boundary: This record audits a capped retrieval-order sample of public CFPB complaint cases. It adds case-level route timing and visibility fields to aggregate complaint evidence, but it does not estimate consumer harm, remedy adequacy, account-level rates, repeat contact, switching, trust, or political action.
